audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Information Science bachelor studies how people and organisations design, use and evaluate digital information systems.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This example follows the Information Systems study path. The three UCR options emphasise software and organisations, data modelling, or human behaviour. Utrecht includes specialist courses and a required individual research project.

cellNotes.text: Both develop computational thinking through Python programming.
Both connect the organisation of data to relational databases. UCR covers SQL, normalisation and query processing.
Utrecht brings human communication, visual information and computer-mediated exchange into one course. UCR approaches these areas across courses.
Utrecht has a dedicated course in modelling organisational processes.
Both develop approaches to designing and building software. Utrecht focuses on methods for developing information systems. UCR includes programming, testing and code review.
Utrecht studies how digital services and organisations fit together in an ecosystem.
Utrecht has a dedicated product software course covering the technical and commercial sides of software products.
Utrecht has a dedicated information security course. UCR covers related topics in database authorisation and AI ethics.
Both study organisations and their needs. UCR introduces entrepreneurship and core business functions. Utrecht focuses on how organisations use ICT.
Both examine how organisations use digital technology to pursue strategic goals.
Both use research into user needs to guide design. UCR prototypes consumer products. Utrecht focuses on interactive digital systems.
UCR introduces the brain and behaviour, including foundations for studying cognition. Utrecht has a dedicated course on cognition and emotion.
UCR studies how people perceive and act. Utrecht teaches how to design and evaluate usable digital systems.
Utrecht combines people, society and ICT in one course. UCR studies aspects of that relationship through sociology, business and AI ethics.
Both develop empirical research design and analysis.
UCR develops argument and communication through rhetoric. Utrecht develops academic skills for information science.
Utrecht requires an individual 15 EC project after 120 EC and Scientific Research Methods. UCR’s optional independent research is separate from the scheduled courses.
Utrecht students choose 45 EC of profiling electives, including at least 15 EC at intermediate or advanced level. Choices must avoid overlap with other courses.

notes.text: Utrecht integrates computing, organisations and human interaction through a compulsory core, one defined study path and an individual research project. UCR combines related work across departments. It offers programming, software development, data analysis, design and user research, while Utrecht has dedicated courses in process modelling, digital ecosystems, product software, usability and information security.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENBUSI211.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
BENBUSI211.text: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. Students study AI's capabilities and limits, applications across business functions and industries, and effects on labour markets, productivity, innovation and inequality. Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.

BENENTR111.name: Consumer Product Design
BENENTR111.text: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.

BENENTR212.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
BENENTR212.text: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.

BENENTR311.name: Market Research
BENENTR311.text: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas—perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
BENGATE101.text: Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.

Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.
